name: Claude meta-skills
blurb: Skills, CLAUDE.md, hooks, subagents, plans and context: set Claude up to do long tasks well.
searches: Claude Code new hook event or skill feature release
agent skill authoring best practices SKILL.md description triggering
Claude Code subagent orchestration workflow new skill
long-running agent context compaction memory planning files technique

tests.prompt: Turn what we just did into a skill: every time we deploy this Next.js app we run `pnpm build`, then `pnpm db:migrate` against the staging DB using DATABASE_URL_STAGING, then smoke-test /api/health. Write the SKILL.md and say where it should live.
tests.good: Project-scoped path (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md); name lowercase-hyphen matching folder; description states scope plus concrete triggers without summarising the steps; ordered steps each with a checkable result; env var named but no secret value; gotchas / what-didn't-work section; mentions testing it on a realistic prompt.

tests.prompt: I keep worrying Claude will run git push --force or rm -rf in my repo. Set up something that reliably stops that in this project.
tests.good: Uses a PreToolUse hook on Bash in .claude/settings.json (merged, not overwritten), not a CLAUDE.md line; script reads tool_input.command with jq and exits 2 with a stderr reason for matches; asks or states project vs global scope; shows a test command (echo JSON | script, expect exit 2) and notes hooks load at session start (/hooks or restart).

tests.prompt: We're starting a 2-day refactor of our billing module with lots of steps. How should we run this so you don't lose track when the context fills up?
tests.good: Proposes a written plan/spec plus on-disk progress files (task_plan/findings/progress or a ledger) with goal, phases, decisions and next step; compacts at phase boundaries after writing state, not mid-implementation; acceptance gates or verification commands per task; optionally subagent-per-task with reviews; final verification before claiming done.

tests.prompt: Write a Claude Code skill for our weekly release that checks deploy status through a small MCP server we still need to build (it reads our status API with a token in DEPLOY_TOKEN). Also make sure Claude can't run scripts/release.sh unless RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md exists.
tests.good: States a short plan first: skill and guard here (skill-authoring.md, hooks-and-guardrails.md, skill-testing-and-triggering.md), the server through ai-agents (mcp-servers.md and tool-design.md: a few read-only tools with clear names, schemas and actionable errors), the token through security (secrets.md: read from the environment, never written into the skill, config or logs). The description gives scope and triggers with no workflow summary; the PreToolUse hook exits 2 with a reason and is tested with sample input; a baseline run without the skill comes first; checks the Done means of all three crafts and says what wasn't run.

tests.prompt: Our team of eight has three skills (release-notes, db-migrate, pr-checklist), one subagent and a PreToolUse hook that blocks `git push --force`, all sitting in my repo's .claude/ folder. Package them as one Claude Code plugin and set it up so everyone on the team can install it from a private GitHub repo with /plugin install, and so it gets enabled automatically when they open our main repo.
tests.good: Plugin root has .claude-plugin/plugin.json (name, version, description) with skills/<name>/SKILL.md, agents/, and hooks/hooks.json at the plugin root, not inside .claude-plugin/; the hook command uses ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} instead of an absolute or repo-relative path and the guard script is executable and exits 2 on a match; a marketplace file .claude-plugin/marketplace.json lists the plugin with a relative or GitHub source, and install commands are /plugin marketplace add <owner>/<repo> then /plugin install <plugin>@<marketplace>; auto-enable is done by committing project settings (.claude/settings.json marketplace and enabled-plugin entries) and Only for a plugin whose marketplace entry has an external source (e.g. its own GitHub repo): committing enabledPlugins in .claude/settings.json shows 'enabled in project settings but isn't installed' until each teammate runs `claude plugin install <plugin>@<marketplace> --scope project`. A plugin with a relative-path source loads from the marketplace copy once the folder is trusted, with no per-teammate install.; says skills become namespaced (/plugin:skill) and tests locally with --plugin-dir and claude plugin validate before publishing; no secrets or tokens in the plugin, scripts reviewed since plugins run with user privileges, and asks before pushing or making the repo visible to others.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.why: Most-used AI coding agent in JetBrains' May-July 2026 survey of 15,000+ developers (39% overall, 71% among regular agent users).

tools.name: Agent Skills (SKILL.md format)
tools.why: Open format started by Anthropic and now supported by 40+ clients incl. Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode (agentskills.io client showcase).

tools.name: AGENTS.md
tools.why: Cross-vendor instruction file used by 60,000+ open-source projects and read by Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Aider, Zed; stewarded by the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (agents.md).

tools.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
tools.why: Open standard for connecting agents to tools, supported by Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor; moved to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation in Dec 2025.

tools.name: Claude Code plugins and marketplaces
tools.why: The distribution unit for skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers in Claude Code; Anthropic's official marketplace is added by default and plugins such as frontend-design have 1M+ installs (vibecoding/Composio round-ups).

tools.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
tools.why: 16% of professional developers in the JetBrains 2026 survey, up from 3% in January, already 60% of Cursor's usage; open source (openai/codex, 128k stars).

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.why: 21% of professional developers and 46% of regular agent users in the JetBrains 2026 survey; reads .github/skills, .claude/skills, .agents/skills, AGENTS.md and copilot-instructions.md.

tools.name: Cursor
tools.why: 12% of professional developers and 39% of regular agent users in the JetBrains 2026 survey; rules in .cursor/rules, AGENTS.md and Agent Skills (.cursor/skills, .agents/skills, .claude/skills).

tools.name: skills.sh and the npx skills CLI
tools.why: Vercel-run directory and installer: find-skills alone has 3.7M installs and the leaderboard lists 1.5M+ installs across agents (skills.sh); works with Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf.

tools.name: Claude Agent SDK
tools.why: Official Python and TypeScript library running the Claude Code loop with hooks, subagents, skills, MCP and CLAUDE.md loading; the GitHub Action is built on it (Anthropic docs).

tools.name: Claude Skills on claude.ai and the Skills API
tools.why: The route for non-Claude-Code users: zip upload under Settings > Features on claude.ai and /v1/skills with container.skills on the API; custom skills do not sync across surfaces (Anthropic docs).

tools.name: Claude Code GitHub Actions
tools.why: Official action (anthropics/claude-code-action, 9k stars) for @claude mentions, scheduled runs and skill/plugin execution in CI.

tools.name: GitHub Spec Kit
tools.why: 140k-star GitHub toolkit for spec-driven development (specify, plan, tasks, implement) with 38 agent integrations (github/spec-kit).

tools.name: Gemini CLI
tools.why: Open-source (107k stars) Google agent that supports Agent Skills and GEMINI.md; in the ~10% 'up-and-coming' group of JetBrains' 2026 survey with OpenCode and Antigravity.

tools.name: OpenCode
tools.why: 211k-star open-source agent used by ~7% of professional developers (JetBrains 2026); reads .opencode/skills and also .claude/skills and .agents/skills.

tools.name: Superpowers plugin
tools.why: Second most-installed Claude Code plugin with 1,009,371 installs on Anthropic's plugin directory (claude.com/plugins/superpowers, Oct 2026) and 295k GitHub stars; the default brainstorm -> spec -> plan -> subagent execution methodology many practitioners run.

tools.name: JetBrains Junie
tools.why: JetBrains AI (IDEs and/or Junie) is used by 9% of professional developers in JetBrains' May-July 2026 survey, above the listed OpenCode (7%); reads .junie/AGENTS.md, root AGENTS.md plus .junie/rules/*.md, legacy .junie/guidelines.md, and ~/.junie/AGENTS.md globally.

tools.name: Google Antigravity
tools.why: 6% of professional developers worldwide and 15% in India in JetBrains' May-July 2026 survey; supports Agent Skills in .agents/skills/ (global ~/.gemini/config/skills/), always-on rules in .agents/rules/, and is migrating workflows to skills.
